summary.headline: Batliboi FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR440 crores with PAT of about INR7 crores, and order backlog stood at INR593 crores.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of about INR440 crores, up 7%, with EBITDA margins described as stable despite supply-chain disruption and macro uncertainty. PAT was about INR7 crores, which management attributed to two one-time items: provisioning for the four labour codes notified in November 2025 and the accounting impact of the merger of Batliboi Environmental Engineering Limited with Batliboi, completed in Q1 FY26. FY26 order inflow was about INR990 crores and backlog at March 2026 was about INR593 crores. Management expects improved top-line and bottom-line in FY27, subject to no further adverse impact from a prolonged Middle East conflict.

financial_highlights.change: Impacted by labour code provisioning and merger accounting impact (management called both one-time)
Prior year about INR339 crores (per analyst citation, confirmed by management as roughly INR600 crores)
Management intends to sustain this level
INR13 crores recorded in Q4 FY26

segments.name: Machine tools
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 order inflow about INR60 crores; backlog INR163 crores at March 2026 (27% of company backlog). 115 machines installed from the Udhna factory.

segments.name: Quickmill (Canada)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR127 crores and Q4 turnover INR35 crores; management expects a much better FY27 based on orders on hand at 1 April 2026.

segments.name: Textile machinery
segments.commentary: FY26 order inflow INR435 crores (Q4 INR38 crores); backlog INR238 crores; FY26 revenue INR50 crores, of which INR13 crores in Q4. Management cited challenges with overseas partners in knitting and spinning, now said to be overcome.

segments.name: Air / environmental engineering
segments.commentary: Air Engineering: Q4 revenue INR17 crores, FY26 INR57 crores, Q4 order inflow INR17 crores, FY26 INR67 crores. Environmental Engineering: Q4 order inflow INR17 crores, Q4 revenue about INR35 crores, backlog INR32 crores.

segments.name: Bioconserve Renewables Envirotech (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: In its first year of operation; management said FY26 profits were good and FY27 performance is expected to be better. Focus is on Zero Liquid Discharge and textile ETP and O&M contracts. No project wins quantified.

guidance_outlook: Management expects improved top-line and bottom-line in FY27, subject to no further adverse impact from a prolonged Middle East conflict.
Quickmill expected to deliver much better performance in FY27 on orders on hand as of 1 April 2026.
Total capex of about INR10 crores planned for FY27.
Canada expansion for Quickmill planned at about CAD 4 million (roughly INR25-30 crores), pending municipal approvals expected in the next two quarters.
Green hydrogen: management expects to convert some of the active inquiries (balance-of-plant and electrolyser) in the next two to three quarters, without quantified revenue.
capex_capacity: FY26 cumulative capex of INR27 crores, mostly in the machine tool division at Surat; benefits started from Q4 FY26.
FY27 planned capex about INR10 crores.
Fan division production capacity up about 40% in FY26.
Textile/Air Engineering plant capacity judged sufficient for expected export volumes; focus is on productivity and quality.
Quickmill expansion in Canada (about CAD 4 million) awaiting municipal permissions.
demand_pricing: Management cites a global CNC market of about US$95 billion in 2024, projected to reach US$195 billion by 2032 (9.9% CAGR).
Indian machine tool sector expected to grow by US$3 billion at over 11% CAGR from 2024 to 2029.
Textile sector revival cited; processing segment described as high growth, driving demand for ZLD and efficiency tools.
Export business is 100% covered by letters of credit, per management; domestic terms vary by division and debtors are rising with the Environmental Engineering business.
Management said order backlog reported (INR593 crores) excludes indirect sales booked, where only commission is recognised as revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What are Bioconserve Renewables' FY27 projections for sales and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said performance will improve on FY26, which was its first year, with no numbers given. It cited good demand for its products and services.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of green hydrogen business and MOUs?
qa_highlights.answer: A balance-of-plant MOU was signed with L&T at a nascent stage. Two to three active inquiries are being pursued, and an MOU was signed with a Chinese electrolyser maker a couple of months ago. Management hopes to convert these in the next two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Export debtors and Bangladesh exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all export business is covered 100% by letters of credit, so no bad debt is expected. Domestic terms vary by division and debtors will rise as Environmental Engineering grows.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the order backlog differ from order inflow minus revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue excludes indirect sales, where only commission is booked. Backlog includes both direct and indirect business. Management pointed to the total business handled figure at the bottom of the quarterly results.

qa_highlights.question: Operating margin of about 7% and plans to improve it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should improve with volume, since overhead is not expanding. It cited ongoing plant-level efficiency work and IT/AI tools for offices. No margin target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Batliboi lag peers such as Jyoti?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Jyoti is a machine tool-only company and is much larger in that business. Batliboi's French or Canadian operations are not separated from Indian ones at Jyoti, and management did not give a peer comparison beyond that.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and elevated energy prices, which management flagged as a condition on its FY27 outlook.
Rising debtors as the domestic Environmental Engineering business grows.
Restructuring of overseas textile machinery partners in knitting and spinning.
Quickmill expansion depends on Canadian municipal permissions; Quickmill is running near full capacity.
Green hydrogen inquiries are at an early stage with no firm orders disclosed.
Backlog definition excludes indirect business; investors asked for separate disclosure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 recovery and order momentum, but hedged with a repeated Middle East conflict caveat. Evasive on segment profitability, bioconserve projections, and peer comparison, where answers were general.
key_quotes: The best years for Batliboi lie ahead.
We view these as one -time adjustments that do not reflect the underlying earnings trajectory of the business.
all our business, export business, is covered under letters of credit, 100%.
we are waiting for permissions from their municipal corporations and the local city government for this expansion, which we hope we will get in the next two quarters.

adds.what: Canada expansion for Quickmill at about CAD 4 million (roughly INR25-30 crores), awaiting municipal approvals

growth.why: Management guides improved top-line and bottom-line in FY27 (no numbers), backed by FY26 order inflow of about INR990 crores, March 2026 backlog of about INR593 crores, Quickmill orders on hand at 1 April 2026, and Surat machine-tool capacity live since Q4 FY26; the Canada CAD 4 million expansion is still awaiting municipal approval.
